# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Mutable run state.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

T1_TMP=""
T1_BACKUPS_TAKEN=0
T1_PATCHES_INSTALLED=0
T1_TRACKED_PIDS=()
T1_TRACKED_PGIDS=()
T1_BLOCK_REASON=""
T1_MARKER=""
T1_FINISHED=0

t1_receipt() { print -r -- "$1" > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$2" }

t1_block() {
  # First reason wins. A later custody failure never overwrites the safety stop
  # that caused it, and a scientific marker can never overwrite a block.
  [[ -z "$T1_BLOCK_REASON" ]] && T1_BLOCK_REASON="$1"
  print -r -- "$1" >> "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-block-reasons.out"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Descendant tracking, termination and reaping.
#
# Each cell runs in its OWN process group, so the whole subtree — Vitest, its
# fork pool, embedded PostgreSQL, worker threads' host processes — can be
# signalled as a unit. The wrapper's own PID is never in that group, which is
# why the final custody check can ask "are exactly these PGIDs gone?" instead of
# a host-wide `pgrep -f T1-3worker-ab` that would match this script, the editor
# that has it open and any unrelated work on the machine.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

t1_track() {
  T1_TRACKED_PIDS+=("$1")
  local pgid
  pgid=$(ps -o pgid= -p "$1" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ')
  [[ -n "$pgid" ]] && T1_TRACKED_PGIDS+=("$pgid")
}

t1_terminate_descendants() {
  local pgid
  for pgid in ${T1_TRACKED_PGIDS[@]}; do
    kill -TERM -"$pgid" 2>/dev/null
  done
  # A bounded grace period, then KILL. Sleeping is acceptable here precisely
  # because nothing else in this wrapper is running concurrently at this point.
  local waited=0
  while (( waited < 20 )); do
    local alive=0
    for pgid in ${T1_TRACKED_PGIDS[@]}; do
      kill -0 -"$pgid" 2>/dev/null && alive=1
    done
    (( alive == 0 )) && break
    sleep 0.5
    (( waited += 1 ))
  done
  for pgid in ${T1_TRACKED_PGIDS[@]}; do
    kill -KILL -"$pgid" 2>/dev/null
  done
  # Reap: the wrapper owns these jobs, so an unreaped zombie is the wrapper's.
  wait 2>/dev/null
}

t1_verify_descendants_gone() {
  local receipt="$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-descendants.out"
  : > "$receipt"
  local gone=0
  local pgid
  for pgid in ${T1_TRACKED_PGIDS[@]}; do
    if kill -0 -"$pgid" 2>/dev/null; then
      print -r -- "PGID=$pgid ALIVE" >> "$receipt"
    else
      print -r -- "PGID=$pgid GONE" >> "$receipt"
      (( gone += 1 ))
    fi
  done
  local pid
  for pid in ${T1_TRACKED_PIDS[@]}; do
    if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
      print -r -- "PID=$pid ALIVE" >> "$receipt"
    else
      print -r -- "PID=$pid GONE" >> "$receipt"
    fi
  done
  print -r -- "TRACKED_DESCENDANTS_GONE=$gone" >> "$receipt"
  grep -q "ALIVE" "$receipt" && return 1
  return 0
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Foreground cell execution.
#
# Foreground in the sense that matters: the wrapper waits for it and nothing
# else runs meanwhile. It is started with `setsid`-equivalent job control so it
# owns a process group, and its complete stdout, complete stderr and raw exit
# status land in three separate files.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

t1_run_cell() {
  local name="$1"; shift
  local out="$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name.out"
  local err="$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name.err"
  local sta="$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name.status"
  ( setopt monitor; exec "$@" ) > "$out" 2> "$err" &
  local pid=$!
  t1_track "$pid"
  wait "$pid"
  local status_code=$?
  print -r -- "$status_code" > "$sta"
  return $status_code
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Restoration and the final status override.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

t1_restore() {
  (( T1_BACKUPS_TAKEN == 1 )) || return 0
  local failed=0
  cp -p "$T1_TMP/registration-database.test.ts.bak" "$T1_INTEGRATION_FILE" || failed=1
  cp -p "$T1_TMP/t1-argon2-worker-contract.test.ts.bak" "$T1_ARCHITECTURE_FILE" || failed=1

  cmp "$T1_INTEGRATION_FILE" "$T1_TMP/registration-database.test.ts.bak"
  t1_receipt "$?" "restore-cmp-registration-database.status"
  grep -qx 0 "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-cmp-registration-database.status" || failed=1
  cmp "$T1_ARCHITECTURE_FILE" "$T1_TMP/t1-argon2-worker-contract.test.ts.bak"
  t1_receipt "$?" "restore-cmp-t1-argon2-worker-contract.status"
  grep -qx 0 "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-cmp-t1-argon2-worker-contract.status" || failed=1

  shasum -a 256 "$T1_INTEGRATION_FILE" \
    > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-hash-registration-database.out"
  shasum -a 256 "$T1_ARCHITECTURE_FILE" \
    > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-hash-t1-argon2-worker-contract.out"
  grep -q "$T1_INTEGRATION_SHA" \
    "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-hash-registration-database.out" || failed=1
  grep -q "$T1_ARCHITECTURE_SHA" \
    "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-hash-t1-argon2-worker-contract.out" || failed=1

  stat -f "%N size=%z mtime=%m" "$T1_INTEGRATION_FILE" \
    > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-stat-registration-database.out"
  stat -f "%N size=%z mtime=%m" "$T1_ARCHITECTURE_FILE" \
    > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-stat-t1-argon2-worker-contract.out"

  T1_PATCHES_INSTALLED=0
  return $failed
}

# One exit path for every outcome. Restoration first, custody second, marker
# last — and restoration failure overrides everything that came before it.
t1_finish() {
  (( T1_FINISHED == 1 )) && return
  T1_FINISHED=1
  local incoming="${1:-}"

  t1_terminate_descendants

  if ! t1_restore; then
    print -r -- "CODEX BLOCKED (restoration)"
    [[ -n "$T1_TMP" && -d "$T1_TMP" ]] && rm -rf "$T1_TMP"
    exit 74
  fi

  # Custody re-verification, after restoration and before any marker.
  git rev-parse HEAD > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-head.out" 2>/dev/null
  grep -qx "$T1_HEAD" "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-head.out" || t1_block "custody"
  git diff --cached --name-only > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-index.out" 2>/dev/null
  [[ -s "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-index.out" ]] && t1_block "custody"
  shasum -a 256 ${T1_GOVERNED_PATHS[@]} > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-hashes.out" 2>/dev/null
  cmp -s "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-hashes.out" \
    "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-hashes.out" || t1_block "custody"
  git diff --check > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-whitespace.out" 2>&1
  git status --porcelain > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-worktree.out" 2>/dev/null
  t1_verify_descendants_gone || t1_block "custody"

  if [[ -n "$incoming" ]]; then t1_block "$incoming"; fi

  if [[ -n "$T1_BLOCK_REASON" ]]; then
    print -r -- "CODEX BLOCKED ($T1_BLOCK_REASON)"
    [[ -n "$T1_TMP" && -d "$T1_TMP" ]] && rm -rf "$T1_TMP"
    exit 2
  fi

  # Only a fully clean path may print a scientific marker, and only the one the
  # adjudicator computed.
  print -r -- "$T1_MARKER"
  [[ -n "$T1_TMP" && -d "$T1_TMP" ]] && rm -rf "$T1_TMP"
  exit 0
}

trap 't1_finish "custody"' INT TERM HUP QUIT
trap 't1_finish "custody"' EXIT

t1_vitest_mutant() {
  local name="$1" file="$2" title="$3" workers="$4"
  local anchor="$5" expected="$6" replacement="$7"
  local slug
  [[ "$file" == "$T1_INTEGRATION_FILE" ]] && slug="integration" || slug="architecture"

  cp -p "$file" "$T1_TMP/$name-preimage.ts" || { t1_block "mutant"; t1_finish }

    > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name-preimage-hash.out"

  node "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-mutation-helper.mjs" \
    --source "$T1_TMP/$name-preimage.ts" --destination "$file" \
    --anchor "$anchor" --expected "$expected" --replacement "$replacement" \
    > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name-mutate.out" 2> "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name-mutate.err"

  grep -qx 0 "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name-mutate.status" || { t1_block "mutant"; t1_finish }

  T1_N3_AB_WORKERS="$workers" T1_N3_AB_CELL_ID="$name" NODE_OPTIONS=--expose-gc \

  (( mutant_status == 0 )) && { t1_block "mutant"; t1_finish }

(( $? == 0 )) || { t1_block "mutant"; t1_finish }

t1_adjudicator_mutant() {

  node "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-mutation-helper.mjs" \

  local mutant_status=$?

  "    const hits = [];"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 13. Settle, restore, verify custody, THEN build and adjudicate.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

t1_terminate_descendants
if ! t1_restore; then
  print -r -- "CODEX BLOCKED (restoration)"
  T1_FINISHED=1
  rm -rf "$T1_TMP"
  exit 74
fi

git rev-parse HEAD > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-head.out" 2>/dev/null
grep -qx "$T1_HEAD" "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-head.out" || { t1_block "custody"; t1_finish }
git diff --cached --name-only > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-index.out" 2>/dev/null
[[ -s "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-index.out" ]] && { t1_block "custody"; t1_finish }
shasum -a 256 ${T1_GOVERNED_PATHS[@]} > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-hashes.out" 2>/dev/null
cmp -s "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-hashes.out" \
  "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-hashes.out" || { t1_block "custody"; t1_finish }
git diff --check > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-whitespace.out" 2>&1

  --literal-carrier "$T1_CARRIER" --out "T1-3worker-ab-manifest.json"
(( $? == 0 )) || { t1_block "receipt"; t1_finish }

t1_run_cell "adjudication" node "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-adjudicator.mjs" \
  "T1-3worker-ab-manifest.json" --literal-carrier "$T1_CARRIER"
T1_ADJUDICATION_STATUS=$?

# The adjudicator's OWN stdout and stderr are scanned before its marker is
# believed: a linter that leaked while reporting a clean scan is still a leak.
if grep -q -f "$T1_CARRIER" "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-adjudication.out" \
  "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-adjudication.err" 2>/dev/null; then
  t1_block "secret"
  t1_finish
fi

T1_MARKER=$(tail -n 1 "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-adjudication.out")
case "$T1_MARKER" in
  "THREE-WORKER A/B "*) ;;
  "CODEX BLOCKED ("*) ;;
  *) t1_block "receipt"; t1_finish ;;
esac
if [[ "$T1_MARKER" == "CODEX BLOCKED ("* ]]; then
  t1_block "${${T1_MARKER#CODEX BLOCKED (}%)}"
fi
if (( T1_ADJUDICATION_STATUS != 0 && T1_ADJUDICATION_STATUS != 2 )); then
  t1_block "receipt"
fi

# The carrier is destroyed here, before the single marker is printed and before
# the temporary directory is removed.
rm -f "$T1_CARRIER"

t1_finish
</content>

#!/bin/zsh
# T1 three-worker A/B — diagnostic runner.
#
# AUTHORING STATUS: design evidence for `T1-claude-3worker-ab-draft-packet.md`,
# authored under `T1-claude-3worker-ab-artifact-correction1-packet.md`. NEVER
# EXECUTED by the authoring seat. It becomes runnable only after two Sol xHigh
# reviewers approve this exact source AND V approves execution and records the
# final packet/artifact hashes in an external launch-authority file.
#
# WHAT THIS FILE IS
# The prior draft DESCRIBED signal handling, descendant tracking, the 512 MiB
# stop, unconditional restoration and the status override. A description cannot
# restore a governed test after a SIGINT. This file implements all of them, and
# the implementation is the point: every exit path — normal, failed, blocked,
# signalled — passes through `t1_finish`, which restores first, verifies custody
# second, and only then prints exactly one lawful marker.
#
# TWO ROOTS
# The outer Git root and the checkout root are different directories, and the
# prior draft conflated them: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the outer
# repository does NOT land where `apps/`, `packages/`, `tests/` and `pnpm` live.
# Both are verified here, and every repository-relative command runs after an
# explicit `cd` to the checkout.
#
# USAGE
#   zsh run-claude-T1-3worker-ab-diagnostic.sh <launch-authority.json>
#
# EXIT STATUS
#   0   one lawful scientific marker was printed
#   2   one lawful `CODEX BLOCKED (...)` marker was printed
#   74  custody or restoration failure; overrides every other outcome

set -u
setopt pipefail
unsetopt err_exit          # every cell's raw status must be captured, not fatal
setopt no_unset

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Roots. Verified before anything else, because every later path depends on
#    getting these two right.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

T1_OUTER_ROOT="/Users/vladmihaimiron/Documents/DebateAIRO"
T1_CHECKOUT_ROOT="$T1_OUTER_ROOT/dialectical-engine"
T1_LOGS_REL="docs/missions/2026-08-17-accounts-privacy-security/logs"
T1_LOGS="$T1_CHECKOUT_ROOT/$T1_LOGS_REL"

if [[ ! -d "$T1_OUTER_ROOT/.git" ]]; then
  print -r -- "CODEX BLOCKED (custody)"
  exit 74
fi
if [[ ! -d "$T1_CHECKOUT_ROOT/apps" || ! -d "$T1_CHECKOUT_ROOT/tests" || ! -d "$T1_LOGS" ]]; then
  print -r -- "CODEX BLOCKED (custody)"
  exit 74
fi
cd "$T1_CHECKOUT_ROOT" || { print -r -- "CODEX BLOCKED (custody)"; exit 74 }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Frozen constants.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

T1_HEAD="9801f85d97e4263a7c8311304e29d6a03c4a6d15"
T1_NODE_VERSION="v22.23.1"
T1_INTEGRATION_FILE="tests/integration/registration-database.test.ts"
T1_ARCHITECTURE_FILE="tests/architecture/t1-argon2-worker-contract.test.ts"
T1_INTEGRATION_SHA="7f8a048afaa415f49f340fe2ef15aa2d4140af1bbf3916bddf5353797a295c58"
T1_ARCHITECTURE_SHA="3548b93282011be73310efe8a2eec31638133dc69a1d92a0cf4ffbc36f253ca1"

T1_TITLE_INTEGRATION="T1 N3 AB three-worker credential concurrency diagnostic"
T1_TITLE_RESOURCE="T1 N3 AB architecture resource cell"
T1_TITLE_POSITIVE_CONTROL="T1 N3 AB retained allocation positive control"
T1_TITLE_FAULT_UNCONFIRMED="T1 N3 AB fault unconfirmed death"
T1_TITLE_FAULT_LATE_EXIT="T1 N3 AB fault late exit before close"
T1_TITLE_FAULT_RETRY="T1 N3 AB fault close-time termination retry fulfilled"

# An ARRAY, expanded as "${T1_VITEST_FLAGS[@]}". A scalar relying on word
# splitting is exactly how a flag with an `=` in it silently becomes two
# arguments — or one argument containing a space — under zsh's default settings.
T1_VITEST_FLAGS=(
  --pool=forks
  --poolOptions.forks.singleFork=true
  --no-file-parallelism
  --reporter=verbose
)

# The twelve governed paths, in the exact order the frozen hash list uses.
T1_GOVERNED_PATHS=(
  apps/api/src/index.ts
  apps/api/src/main.ts
  apps/api/src/registration.ts
  packages/crypto/src/index.ts
  packages/crypto/src/argon2-worker.ts
  packages/crypto/src/argon2-worker-pool.ts
  packages/db/src/identity.ts
  packages/register/src/auth-policy.ts
  tests/integration/registration-database.test.ts
  tests/unit/registration.test.ts
  tests/unit/argon2-worker-pool.test.ts
  tests/architecture/t1-argon2-worker-contract.test.ts
)

T1_ARTIFACTS=(
  T1-3worker-ab-booted-rss-harness.mjs
  T1-3worker-ab-adjudicator.mjs
  T1-3worker-ab-command-matrix.md
  T1-3worker-ab-integration.patch
  T1-3worker-ab-architecture.patch
  T1-3worker-ab-mutation-helper.mjs
  T1-3worker-ab-manifest-builder.mjs
  run-claude-T1-3worker-ab-diagnostic.sh
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Mutable run state.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

T1_TMP=""
T1_BACKUPS_TAKEN=0
T1_PATCHES_INSTALLED=0
T1_TRACKED_PIDS=()
T1_TRACKED_PGIDS=()
T1_BLOCK_REASON=""
T1_MARKER=""
T1_FINISHED=0

t1_receipt() { print -r -- "$1" > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$2" }

t1_block() {
  # First reason wins. A later custody failure never overwrites the safety stop
  # that caused it, and a scientific marker can never overwrite a block.
  [[ -z "$T1_BLOCK_REASON" ]] && T1_BLOCK_REASON="$1"
  print -r -- "$1" >> "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-block-reasons.out"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Descendant tracking, termination and reaping.
#
# Each cell runs in its OWN process group, so the whole subtree — Vitest, its
# fork pool, embedded PostgreSQL, worker threads' host processes — can be
# signalled as a unit. The wrapper's own PID is never in that group, which is
# why the final custody check can ask "are exactly these PGIDs gone?" instead of
# a host-wide `pgrep -f T1-3worker-ab` that would match this script, the editor
# that has it open and any unrelated work on the machine.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

t1_track() {
  T1_TRACKED_PIDS+=("$1")
  local pgid
  pgid=$(ps -o pgid= -p "$1" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ')
  [[ -n "$pgid" ]] && T1_TRACKED_PGIDS+=("$pgid")
}

t1_terminate_descendants() {
  local pgid
  for pgid in ${T1_TRACKED_PGIDS[@]}; do
    kill -TERM -"$pgid" 2>/dev/null
  done
  # A bounded grace period, then KILL. Sleeping is acceptable here precisely
  # because nothing else in this wrapper is running concurrently at this point.
  local waited=0
  while (( waited < 20 )); do
    local alive=0
    for pgid in ${T1_TRACKED_PGIDS[@]}; do
      kill -0 -"$pgid" 2>/dev/null && alive=1
    done
    (( alive == 0 )) && break
    sleep 0.5
    (( waited += 1 ))
  done
  for pgid in ${T1_TRACKED_PGIDS[@]}; do
    kill -KILL -"$pgid" 2>/dev/null
  done
  # Reap: the wrapper owns these jobs, so an unreaped zombie is the wrapper's.
  wait 2>/dev/null
}

t1_verify_descendants_gone() {
  local receipt="$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-descendants.out"
  : > "$receipt"
  local gone=0
  local pgid
  for pgid in ${T1_TRACKED_PGIDS[@]}; do
    if kill -0 -"$pgid" 2>/dev/null; then
      print -r -- "PGID=$pgid ALIVE" >> "$receipt"
    else
      print -r -- "PGID=$pgid GONE" >> "$receipt"
      (( gone += 1 ))
    fi
  done
  local pid
  for pid in ${T1_TRACKED_PIDS[@]}; do
    if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
      print -r -- "PID=$pid ALIVE" >> "$receipt"
    else
      print -r -- "PID=$pid GONE" >> "$receipt"
    fi
  done
  print -r -- "TRACKED_DESCENDANTS_GONE=$gone" >> "$receipt"
  grep -q "ALIVE" "$receipt" && return 1
  return 0
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Foreground cell execution.
#
# Foreground in the sense that matters: the wrapper waits for it and nothing
# else runs meanwhile. It is started with `setsid`-equivalent job control so it
# owns a process group, and its complete stdout, complete stderr and raw exit
# status land in three separate files.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

t1_run_cell() {
  local name="$1"; shift
  local out="$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name.out"
  local err="$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name.err"
  local sta="$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name.status"
  ( setopt monitor; exec "$@" ) > "$out" 2> "$err" &
  local pid=$!
  t1_track "$pid"
  wait "$pid"
  local status_code=$?
  print -r -- "$status_code" > "$sta"
  return $status_code
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Restoration and the final status override.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

t1_restore() {
  (( T1_BACKUPS_TAKEN == 1 )) || return 0
  local failed=0
  cp -p "$T1_TMP/registration-database.test.ts.bak" "$T1_INTEGRATION_FILE" || failed=1
  cp -p "$T1_TMP/t1-argon2-worker-contract.test.ts.bak" "$T1_ARCHITECTURE_FILE" || failed=1

  cmp "$T1_INTEGRATION_FILE" "$T1_TMP/registration-database.test.ts.bak"
  t1_receipt "$?" "restore-cmp-registration-database.status"
  grep -qx 0 "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-cmp-registration-database.status" || failed=1
  cmp "$T1_ARCHITECTURE_FILE" "$T1_TMP/t1-argon2-worker-contract.test.ts.bak"
  t1_receipt "$?" "restore-cmp-t1-argon2-worker-contract.status"
  grep -qx 0 "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-cmp-t1-argon2-worker-contract.status" || failed=1

  shasum -a 256 "$T1_INTEGRATION_FILE" \
    > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-hash-registration-database.out"
  shasum -a 256 "$T1_ARCHITECTURE_FILE" \
    > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-hash-t1-argon2-worker-contract.out"
  grep -q "$T1_INTEGRATION_SHA" \
    "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-hash-registration-database.out" || failed=1
  grep -q "$T1_ARCHITECTURE_SHA" \
    "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-hash-t1-argon2-worker-contract.out" || failed=1

  stat -f "%N size=%z mtime=%m" "$T1_INTEGRATION_FILE" \
    > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-stat-registration-database.out"
  stat -f "%N size=%z mtime=%m" "$T1_ARCHITECTURE_FILE" \
    > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-stat-t1-argon2-worker-contract.out"

  T1_PATCHES_INSTALLED=0
  return $failed
}

# One exit path for every outcome. Restoration first, custody second, marker
# last — and restoration failure overrides everything that came before it.
t1_finish() {
  (( T1_FINISHED == 1 )) && return
  T1_FINISHED=1
  local incoming="${1:-}"

  t1_terminate_descendants

  if ! t1_restore; then
    print -r -- "CODEX BLOCKED (restoration)"
    [[ -n "$T1_TMP" && -d "$T1_TMP" ]] && rm -rf "$T1_TMP"
    exit 74
  fi

  # Custody re-verification, after restoration and before any marker.
  git rev-parse HEAD > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-head.out" 2>/dev/null
  grep -qx "$T1_HEAD" "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-head.out" || t1_block "custody"
  git diff --cached --name-only > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-index.out" 2>/dev/null
  [[ -s "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-index.out" ]] && t1_block "custody"
  shasum -a 256 ${T1_GOVERNED_PATHS[@]} > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-hashes.out" 2>/dev/null

t1_vitest_mutant() {

  [[ "$file" == "$T1_INTEGRATION_FILE" ]] && slug="integration" || slug="architecture"

    --source "$T1_TMP/$name-preimage.ts" --destination "$file" \
    --anchor "$anchor" --expected "$expected" --replacement "$replacement" \
    > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name-mutate.out" 2> "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name-mutate.err"
  t1_receipt "$?" "$name-mutate.status"
  grep -qx 0 "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name-mutate.status" || { t1_block "mutant"; t1_finish }

  T1_N3_AB_WORKERS="$workers" T1_N3_AB_CELL_ID="$name" NODE_OPTIONS=--expose-gc \
    t1_run_cell "$name" pnpm exec vitest run "$file" -t "$title" "${T1_VITEST_FLAGS[@]}"
  local mutant_status=$?

  cp -p "$T1_TMP/$name-preimage.ts" "$file"
  cmp "$file" "$T1_TMP/$name-preimage.ts"
  t1_receipt "$?" "$name-restore.status"
  shasum -a 256 "$file" > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name-restore-hash.out"
  stat -f "%N size=%z mtime=%m" "$file" > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name-restore-stat.out"
  grep -qx 0 "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name-restore.status" \
    || { t1_block "restoration"; t1_finish }

  # A mutant that exits 0 has survived. A mutant with no status at all is not a
  # kill either: the builder refuses a missing or malformed status outright.
  (( mutant_status == 0 )) && { t1_block "mutant"; t1_finish }
  return 0
}

git diff --check > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-whitespace.out" 2>&1
git status --porcelain > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-worktree.out" 2>/dev/null
t1_verify_descendants_gone || { t1_block "custody"; t1_finish }

t1_run_cell "manifest-build" node "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-manifest-builder.mjs" \
  --logs "$T1_LOGS" --launch-authority "$T1_AUTHORITY" \
  --literal-carrier "$T1_CARRIER" --out "T1-3worker-ab-manifest.json"
(( $? == 0 )) || { t1_block "receipt"; t1_finish }

t1_run_cell "adjudication" node "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-adjudicator.mjs" \
  "T1-3worker-ab-manifest.json" --literal-carrier "$T1_CARRIER"
T1_ADJUDICATION_STATUS=$?

# The adjudicator's OWN stdout and stderr are scanned before its marker is
# believed: a linter that leaked while reporting a clean scan is still a leak.
if grep -q -f "$T1_CARRIER" "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-adjudication.out" \
  "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-adjudication.err" 2>/dev/null; then
  t1_block "secret"
  t1_finish
fi

T1_MARKER=$(tail -n 1 "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-adjudication.out")
case "$T1_MARKER" in
  "THREE-WORKER A/B "*) ;;
  "CODEX BLOCKED ("*) ;;
  *) t1_block "receipt"; t1_finish ;;
esac
if [[ "$T1_MARKER" == "CODEX BLOCKED ("* ]]; then
  t1_block "${${T1_MARKER#CODEX BLOCKED (}%)}"
fi
if (( T1_ADJUDICATION_STATUS != 0 && T1_ADJUDICATION_STATUS != 2 )); then
  t1_block "receipt"
fi

# The carrier is destroyed here, before the single marker is printed and before
# the temporary directory is removed.
rm -f "$T1_CARRIER"

t1_finish
</content>

#!/bin/zsh
# T1 three-worker A/B — diagnostic runner.
#
# AUTHORING STATUS: design evidence for `T1-claude-3worker-ab-draft-packet.md`,
# authored under `T1-claude-3worker-ab-artifact-correction1-packet.md`. NEVER
# EXECUTED by the authoring seat. It becomes runnable only after two Sol xHigh
# reviewers approve this exact source AND V approves execution and records the
# final packet/artifact hashes in an external launch-authority file.
#
# WHAT THIS FILE IS
# The prior draft DESCRIBED signal handling, descendant tracking, the 512 MiB
# stop, unconditional restoration and the status override. A description cannot
# restore a governed test after a SIGINT. This file implements all of them, and
# the implementation is the point: every exit path — normal, failed, blocked,
# signalled — passes through `t1_finish`, which restores first, verifies custody
# second, and only then prints exactly one lawful marker.
#
# TWO ROOTS
# The outer Git root and the checkout root are different directories, and the
# prior draft conflated them: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the outer
# repository does NOT land where `apps/`, `packages/`, `tests/` and `pnpm` live.
# Both are verified here, and every repository-relative command runs after an
# explicit `cd` to the checkout.
#
# USAGE
#   zsh run-claude-T1-3worker-ab-diagnostic.sh <launch-authority.json>
#
# EXIT STATUS
#   0   one lawful scientific marker was printed
#   2   one lawful `CODEX BLOCKED (...)` marker was printed
#   74  custody or restoration failure; overrides every other outcome

set -u
setopt pipefail
unsetopt err_exit          # every cell's raw status must be captured, not fatal
setopt no_unset

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Roots. Verified before anything else, because every later path depends on
#    getting these two right.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

T1_OUTER_ROOT="/Users/vladmihaimiron/Documents/DebateAIRO"
T1_CHECKOUT_ROOT="$T1_OUTER_ROOT/dialectical-engine"
T1_LOGS_REL="docs/missions/2026-08-17-accounts-privacy-security/logs"
T1_LOGS="$T1_CHECKOUT_ROOT/$T1_LOGS_REL"

if [[ ! -d "$T1_OUTER_ROOT/.git" ]]; then
  print -r -- "CODEX BLOCKED (custody)"
  exit 74
fi
if [[ ! -d "$T1_CHECKOUT_ROOT/apps" || ! -d "$T1_CHECKOUT_ROOT/tests" || ! -d "$T1_LOGS" ]]; then
  print -r -- "CODEX BLOCKED (custody)"
  exit 74
fi
cd "$T1_CHECKOUT_ROOT" || { print -r -- "CODEX BLOCKED (custody)"; exit 74 }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Frozen constants.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

T1_HEAD="9801f85d97e4263a7c8311304e29d6a03c4a6d15"
T1_NODE_VERSION="v22.23.1"
T1_INTEGRATION_FILE="tests/integration/registration-database.test.ts"
T1_ARCHITECTURE_FILE="tests/architecture/t1-argon2-worker-contract.test.ts"
T1_INTEGRATION_SHA="7f8a048afaa415f49f340fe2ef15aa2d4140af1bbf3916bddf5353797a295c58"
T1_ARCHITECTURE_SHA="3548b93282011be73310efe8a2eec31638133dc69a1d92a0cf4ffbc36f253ca1"

T1_TITLE_INTEGRATION="T1 N3 AB three-worker credential concurrency diagnostic"
T1_TITLE_RESOURCE="T1 N3 AB architecture resource cell"
T1_TITLE_POSITIVE_CONTROL="T1 N3 AB retained allocation positive control"
T1_TITLE_FAULT_UNCONFIRMED="T1 N3 AB fault unconfirmed death"
T1_TITLE_FAULT_LATE_EXIT="T1 N3 AB fault late exit before close"
T1_TITLE_FAULT_RETRY="T1 N3 AB fault close-time termination retry fulfilled"

# An ARRAY, expanded as "${T1_VITEST_FLAGS[@]}". A scalar relying on word
# splitting is exactly how a flag with an `=` in it silently becomes two
# arguments — or one argument containing a space — under zsh's default settings.
T1_VITEST_FLAGS=(
  --pool=forks
  --poolOptions.forks.singleFork=true
  --no-file-parallelism
  --reporter=verbose
)

# The twelve governed paths, in the exact order the frozen hash list uses.
T1_GOVERNED_PATHS=(
  apps/api/src/index.ts
  apps/api/src/main.ts
  apps/api/src/registration.ts
  packages/crypto/src/index.ts
  packages/crypto/src/argon2-worker.ts
  packages/crypto/src/argon2-worker-pool.ts
  packages/db/src/identity.ts
  packages/register/src/auth-policy.ts
  tests/integration/registration-database.test.ts
  tests/unit/registration.test.ts
  tests/unit/argon2-worker-pool.test.ts
  tests/architecture/t1-argon2-worker-contract.test.ts
)

T1_ARTIFACTS=(
  T1-3worker-ab-booted-rss-harness.mjs
  T1-3worker-ab-adjudicator.mjs
  T1-3worker-ab-command-matrix.md
  T1-3worker-ab-integration.patch
  T1-3worker-ab-architecture.patch
  T1-3worker-ab-mutation-helper.mjs
  T1-3worker-ab-manifest-builder.mjs
  run-claude-T1-3worker-ab-diagnostic.sh
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Mutable run state.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

T1_TMP=""
T1_BACKUPS_TAKEN=0
T1_PATCHES_INSTALLED=0
T1_TRACKED_PIDS=()
T1_TRACKED_PGIDS=()
T1_BLOCK_REASON=""
T1_MARKER=""
T1_FINISHED=0

t1_receipt() { print -r -- "$1" > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$2" }

t1_block() {
  # First reason wins. A later custody failure never overwrites the safety stop
  # that caused it, and a scientific marker can never overwrite a block.
  [[ -z "$T1_BLOCK_REASON" ]] && T1_BLOCK_REASON="$1"
  print -r -- "$1" >> "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-block-reasons.out"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Descendant tracking, termination and reaping.
#
# Each cell runs in its OWN process group, so the whole subtree — Vitest, its
# fork pool, embedded PostgreSQL, worker threads' host processes — can be
# signalled as a unit. The wrapper's own PID is never in that group, which is
# why the final custody check can ask "are exactly these PGIDs gone?" instead of
# a host-wide `pgrep -f T1-3worker-ab` that would match this script, the editor
# that has it open and any unrelated work on the machine.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

t1_track() {
  T1_TRACKED_PIDS+=("$1")
  local pgid
  pgid=$(ps -o pgid= -p "$1" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ')
  [[ -n "$pgid" ]] && T1_TRACKED_PGIDS+=("$pgid")
}

t1_terminate_descendants() {
  local pgid
  for pgid in ${T1_TRACKED_PGIDS[@]}; do
    kill -TERM -"$pgid" 2>/dev/null
  done
  # A bounded grace period, then KILL. Sleeping is acceptable here precisely
  # because nothing else in this wrapper is running concurrently at this point.
  local waited=0
  while (( waited < 20 )); do
    local alive=0
    for pgid in ${T1_TRACKED_PGIDS[@]}; do
      kill -0 -"$pgid" 2>/dev/null && alive=1
    done
    (( alive == 0 )) && break
    sleep 0.5
    (( waited += 1 ))
  done
  for pgid in ${T1_TRACKED_PGIDS[@]}; do
    kill -KILL -"$pgid" 2>/dev/null
  done
  # Reap: the wrapper owns these jobs, so an unreaped zombie is the wrapper's.
  wait 2>/dev/null
}

t1_verify_descendants_gone() {
  local receipt="$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-descendants.out"
  : > "$receipt"
  local gone=0
  local pgid
  for pgid in ${T1_TRACKED_PGIDS[@]}; do
    if kill -0 -"$pgid" 2>/dev/null; then
      print -r -- "PGID=$pgid ALIVE" >> "$receipt"
    else
      print -r -- "PGID=$pgid GONE" >> "$receipt"
      (( gone += 1 ))
    fi
  done
  local pid
  for pid in ${T1_TRACKED_PIDS[@]}; do
    if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
      print -r -- "PID=$pid ALIVE" >> "$receipt"
    else
      print -r -- "PID=$pid GONE" >> "$receipt"
    fi
  done
  print -r -- "TRACKED_DESCENDANTS_GONE=$gone" >> "$receipt"
  grep -q "ALIVE" "$receipt" && return 1
  return 0
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Foreground cell execution.
#
# Foreground in the sense that matters: the wrapper waits for it and nothing
# else runs meanwhile. It is started with `setsid`-equivalent job control so it
# owns a process group, and its complete stdout, complete stderr and raw exit
# status land in three separate files.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

t1_run_cell() {
  local name="$1"; shift
  local out="$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name.out"
  local err="$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name.err"
  local sta="$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name.status"
  ( setopt monitor; exec "$@" ) > "$out" 2> "$err" &
  local pid=$!
  t1_track "$pid"
  wait "$pid"
  local status_code=$?
  print -r -- "$status_code" > "$sta"
  return $status_code
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Restoration and the final status override.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

t1_restore() {
  (( T1_BACKUPS_TAKEN == 1 )) || return 0
  local failed=0
  cp -p "$T1_TMP/registration-database.test.ts.bak" "$T1_INTEGRATION_FILE" || failed=1
  cp -p "$T1_TMP/t1-argon2-worker-contract.test.ts.bak" "$T1_ARCHITECTURE_FILE" || failed=1

  cmp "$T1_INTEGRATION_FILE" "$T1_TMP/registration-database.test.ts.bak"
  t1_receipt "$?" "restore-cmp-registration-database.status"
  grep -qx 0 "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-cmp-registration-database.status" || failed=1
  cmp "$T1_ARCHITECTURE_FILE" "$T1_TMP/t1-argon2-worker-contract.test.ts.bak"
  t1_receipt "$?" "restore-cmp-t1-argon2-worker-contract.status"
  grep -qx 0 "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-cmp-t1-argon2-worker-contract.status" || failed=1

  shasum -a 256 "$T1_INTEGRATION_FILE" \
    > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-hash-registration-database.out"
  shasum -a 256 "$T1_ARCHITECTURE_FILE" \
    > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-hash-t1-argon2-worker-contract.out"
  grep -q "$T1_INTEGRATION_SHA" \
    "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-hash-registration-database.out" || failed=1
  grep -q "$T1_ARCHITECTURE_SHA" \
    "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-hash-t1-argon2-worker-contract.out" || failed=1

  stat -f "%N size=%z mtime=%m" "$T1_INTEGRATION_FILE" \
    > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-stat-registration-database.out"
  stat -f "%N size=%z mtime=%m" "$T1_ARCHITECTURE_FILE" \
    > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-stat-t1-argon2-worker-contract.out"

  T1_PATCHES_INSTALLED=0
  return $failed
}

# One exit path for every outcome. Restoration first, custody second, marker
# last — and restoration failure overrides everything that came before it.
t1_finish() {
  (( T1_FINISHED == 1 )) && return
  T1_FINISHED=1
  local incoming="${1:-}"

  t1_terminate_descendants

  if ! t1_restore; then
    print -r -- "CODEX BLOCKED (restoration)"
    [[ -n "$T1_TMP" && -d "$T1_TMP" ]] && rm -rf "$T1_TMP"
    exit 74
  fi

  # Custody re-verification, after restoration and before any marker.
  git rev-parse HEAD > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-head.out" 2>/dev/null
  grep -qx "$T1_HEAD" "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-head.out" || t1_block "custody"
  git diff --cached --name-only > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-index.out" 2>/dev/null
  [[ -s "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-index.out" ]] && t1_block "custody"
  shasum -a 256 ${T1_GOVERNED_PATHS[@]} > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-hashes.out" 2>/dev/null
  cmp -s "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-hashes.out" \
    "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-hashes.out" || t1_block "custody"
  git diff --check > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-whitespace.out" 2>&1
  git status --porcelain > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-worktree.out" 2>/dev/null
  t1_verify_descendants_gone || t1_block "custody"

  if [[ -n "$incoming" ]]; then t1_block "$incoming"; fi

  if [[ -n "$T1_BLOCK_REASON" ]]; then
    print -r -- "CODEX BLOCKED ($T1_BLOCK_REASON)"
    [[ -n "$T1_TMP" && -d "$T1_TMP" ]] && rm -rf "$T1_TMP"
    exit 2
  fi

  # Only a fully clean path may print a scientific marker, and only the one the
  # adjudicator computed.
  print -r -- "$T1_MARKER"
  [[ -n "$T1_TMP" && -d "$T1_TMP" ]] && rm -rf "$T1_TMP"
  exit 0
}

trap 't1_finish "custody"' INT TERM HUP QUIT
trap 't1_finish "custody"' EXIT

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. External launch authority. Absence or mismatch stops BEFORE any backup or
#    edit — the seat must never have touched a governed file on this path.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

T1_AUTHORITY="${1:-}"
if [[ -z "$T1_AUTHORITY" || ! -r "$T1_AUTHORITY" ]]; then
  t1_finish "custody"
fi
T1_PACKET_SHA=$(/usr/bin/sed -n 's/.*"packetSha256"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([0-9a-f]\{64\}\)".*/\1/p' \
  "$T1_AUTHORITY" | head -n 1)
[[ ${#T1_PACKET_SHA} -eq 64 ]] || t1_finish "custody"

shasum -a 256 "$T1_LOGS/T1-claude-3worker-ab-draft-packet.md" \
  > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-packet.out" 2>/dev/null
t1_receipt "$?" "preflight-packet.status"
grep -q "$T1_PACKET_SHA" "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-packet.out" || t1_finish "custody"

# Every artifact, recomputed and compared to the authority's exact value.
: > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-artifacts.out"
for artifact in ${T1_ARTIFACTS[@]}; do
  observed=$(shasum -a 256 "$T1_LOGS/$artifact" 2>/dev/null | cut -d' ' -f1)
  print -r -- "$observed  $artifact" >> "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-artifacts.out"
  grep -q "\"$artifact\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\"$observed\"" "$T1_AUTHORITY" \
    || t1_finish "custody"
done
t1_receipt "0" "preflight-artifacts.status"

export T1_N3_AB_PACKET_SHA256="$T1_PACKET_SHA"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Frozen preflight. Every comparison is an executable gate with a receipt.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

git rev-parse --show-toplevel > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-toplevel.out" 2>/dev/null
t1_receipt "$?" "preflight-toplevel.status"
grep -qx "$T1_OUTER_ROOT" "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-toplevel.out" || t1_finish "custody"

print -r -- "$PWD" > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-checkout.out"
grep -qx "$T1_CHECKOUT_ROOT" "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-checkout.out" || t1_finish "custody"

git rev-parse HEAD > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-head.out" 2>/dev/null
t1_receipt "$?" "preflight-head.status"
grep -qx "$T1_HEAD" "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-head.out" || t1_finish "custody"

git diff --cached --name-only > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-index.out" 2>/dev/null
t1_receipt "$?" "preflight-index.status"
[[ -s "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-index.out" ]] && t1_finish "custody"

shasum -a 256 ${T1_GOVERNED_PATHS[@]} > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-hashes.out" 2>/dev/null
t1_receipt "$?" "preflight-hashes.status"
for path in ${T1_GOVERNED_PATHS[@]}; do
  grep -q "  $path\$" "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-hashes.out" || t1_finish "custody"
done
[[ $(wc -l < "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-hashes.out") -eq 12 ]] || t1_finish "custody"

# The authorized entry baseline: the worktree state this run inherited. Custody
# at the end is "baseline plus the named new receipts", never "absolutely clean".
git status --porcelain > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-entry-worktree-baseline.out" 2>/dev/null
t1_receipt "$?" "entry-worktree-baseline.status"

node --version > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-node.out" 2>/dev/null
t1_receipt "$?" "preflight-node.status"
grep -qx "$T1_NODE_VERSION" "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-node.out" || t1_finish "custody"

# Every Vitest flag asserted against the pinned runner's own help output.
pnpm exec vitest --help > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-vitest-flags.out" 2>&1
t1_receipt "$?" "preflight-vitest-flags.status"
for flag in ${T1_VITEST_FLAGS[@]}; do
  grep -q -- "${flag%%=*}" "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-vitest-flags.out" || t1_finish "custody"
done

for source in T1-3worker-ab-booted-rss-harness.mjs T1-3worker-ab-adjudicator.mjs \
  T1-3worker-ab-mutation-helper.mjs T1-3worker-ab-manifest-builder.mjs; do
  node --check "$T1_LOGS/$source" > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-syntax-$source.out" 2>&1
  t1_receipt "$?" "preflight-syntax-$source.status"
  grep -qx 0 "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-syntax-$source.status" || t1_finish "custody"
done

zsh -n "$T1_LOGS/run-claude-T1-3worker-ab-diagnostic.sh" \
  > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-wrapper-syntax.out" 2>&1
t1_receipt "$?" "preflight-wrapper-syntax.status"
grep -qx 0 "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-wrapper-syntax.status" || t1_finish "custody"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Unique temporary directory, two `cp -p` backups, verified trap arming.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

T1_TMP="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/t1-n3-ab-XXXXXXXX")" || t1_finish "custody"
chmod 700 "$T1_TMP"
T1_CARRIER="$T1_TMP/generated-literals.txt"
: > "$T1_CARRIER"
chmod 600 "$T1_CARRIER"

cp -p "$T1_INTEGRATION_FILE" "$T1_TMP/registration-database.test.ts.bak"
t1_receipt "$?" "backup-integration.status"
grep -qx 0 "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-backup-integration.status" || t1_finish "custody"
cp -p "$T1_ARCHITECTURE_FILE" "$T1_TMP/t1-argon2-worker-contract.test.ts.bak"
t1_receipt "$?" "backup-architecture.status"
grep -qx 0 "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-backup-architecture.status" || t1_finish "custody"
T1_BACKUPS_TAKEN=1

shasum -a 256 "$T1_TMP/registration-database.test.ts.bak" \
  > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-backup-hash-registration-database.out"
shasum -a 256 "$T1_TMP/t1-argon2-worker-contract.test.ts.bak" \
  > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-backup-hash-t1-argon2-worker-contract.out"
grep -q "$T1_INTEGRATION_SHA" \
  "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-backup-hash-registration-database.out" || t1_finish "custody"
grep -q "$T1_ARCHITECTURE_SHA" \
  "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-backup-hash-t1-argon2-worker-contract.out" || t1_finish "custody"

# Trap arming is verified, not assumed: a trap table that lost its entries would
# make every later "restored on any exit" claim false.
trap -p INT > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-trap-arming.out" 2>&1
trap -p TERM >> "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-trap-arming.out" 2>&1

  (( mutant_status == 0 )) && { t1_block "mutant"; t1_finish }
  return 0

if grep -q -f "$T1_CARRIER" "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-adjudication.out" \
  "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-adjudication.err" 2>/dev/null; then
  t1_block "secret"
  t1_finish
fi

T1_MARKER=$(tail -n 1 "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-adjudication.out")
case "$T1_MARKER" in
  "THREE-WORKER A/B "*) ;;
  "CODEX BLOCKED ("*) ;;
  *) t1_block "receipt"; t1_finish ;;
esac
if [[ "$T1_MARKER" == "CODEX BLOCKED ("* ]]; then

fi
if (( T1_ADJUDICATION_STATUS != 0 && T1_ADJUDICATION_STATUS != 2 )); then
  t1_block "receipt"
fi

# The carrier is destroyed here, before the single marker is printed and before
# the temporary directory is removed.

T1_BACKUPS_TAKEN=0
T1_PATCHES_INSTALLED=0
T1_TRACKED_PIDS=()
T1_TRACKED_PGIDS=()
T1_BLOCK_REASON=""
T1_MARKER=""
T1_FINISHED=0

t1_receipt() { print -r -- "$1" > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$2" }

t1_block() {
  # First reason wins. A later custody failure never overwrites the safety stop
  # that caused it, and a scientific marker can never overwrite a block.
  [[ -z "$T1_BLOCK_REASON" ]] && T1_BLOCK_REASON="$1"
  print -r -- "$1" >> "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-block-reasons.out"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Descendant tracking, termination and reaping.
#
# Each cell runs in its OWN process group, so the whole subtree — Vitest, its
# fork pool, embedded PostgreSQL, worker threads' host processes — can be
# signalled as a unit. The wrapper's own PID is never in that group, which is
# why the final custody check can ask "are exactly these PGIDs gone?" instead of
# a host-wide `pgrep -f T1-3worker-ab` that would match this script, the editor
# that has it open and any unrelated work on the machine.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

t1_track() {
  T1_TRACKED_PIDS+=("$1")
  local pgid
  pgid=$(ps -o pgid= -p "$1" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ')
  [[ -n "$pgid" ]] && T1_TRACKED_PGIDS+=("$pgid")
}

t1_terminate_descendants() {
  local pgid
  for pgid in ${T1_TRACKED_PGIDS[@]}; do
    kill -TERM -"$pgid" 2>/dev/null
  done
  # A bounded grace period, then KILL. Sleeping is acceptable here precisely
  # because nothing else in this wrapper is running concurrently at this point.
  local waited=0
  while (( waited < 20 )); do
    local alive=0
    for pgid in ${T1_TRACKED_PGIDS[@]}; do
      kill -0 -"$pgid" 2>/dev/null && alive=1
    done
    (( alive == 0 )) && break
    sleep 0.5
    (( waited += 1 ))
  done
  for pgid in ${T1_TRACKED_PGIDS[@]}; do
    kill -KILL -"$pgid" 2>/dev/null
  done
  # Reap: the wrapper owns these jobs, so an unreaped zombie is the wrapper's.
  wait 2>/dev/null
}

t1_verify_descendants_gone() {
  local receipt="$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-descendants.out"
  : > "$receipt"
  local gone=0
  local pgid
  for pgid in ${T1_TRACKED_PGIDS[@]}; do
    if kill -0 -"$pgid" 2>/dev/null; then
      print -r -- "PGID=$pgid ALIVE" >> "$receipt"
    else
      print -r -- "PGID=$pgid GONE" >> "$receipt"
      (( gone += 1 ))
    fi
  done
  local pid
  for pid in ${T1_TRACKED_PIDS[@]}; do
    if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
      print -r -- "PID=$pid ALIVE" >> "$receipt"
    else
      print -r -- "PID=$pid GONE" >> "$receipt"
    fi
  done
  print -r -- "TRACKED_DESCENDANTS_GONE=$gone" >> "$receipt"
  grep -q "ALIVE" "$receipt" && return 1
  return 0
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Foreground cell execution.
#
# Foreground in the sense that matters: the wrapper waits for it and nothing
# else runs meanwhile. It is started with `setsid`-equivalent job control so it
# owns a process group, and its complete stdout, complete stderr and raw exit
# status land in three separate files.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

t1_run_cell() {
  local name="$1"; shift
  local out="$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name.out"
  local err="$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name.err"
  local sta="$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name.status"
  ( setopt monitor; exec "$@" ) > "$out" 2> "$err" &
  local pid=$!
  t1_track "$pid"
  wait "$pid"
  local status_code=$?
  print -r -- "$status_code" > "$sta"
  return $status_code
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Restoration and the final status override.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

t1_restore() {
  (( T1_BACKUPS_TAKEN == 1 )) || return 0
  local failed=0
  cp -p "$T1_TMP/registration-database.test.ts.bak" "$T1_INTEGRATION_FILE" || failed=1
  cp -p "$T1_TMP/t1-argon2-worker-contract.test.ts.bak" "$T1_ARCHITECTURE_FILE" || failed=1

  cmp "$T1_INTEGRATION_FILE" "$T1_TMP/registration-database.test.ts.bak"
  t1_receipt "$?" "restore-cmp-registration-database.status"
  grep -qx 0 "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-cmp-registration-database.status" || failed=1
  cmp "$T1_ARCHITECTURE_FILE" "$T1_TMP/t1-argon2-worker-contract.test.ts.bak"
  t1_receipt "$?" "restore-cmp-t1-argon2-worker-contract.status"
  grep -qx 0 "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-cmp-t1-argon2-worker-contract.status" || failed=1

  shasum -a 256 "$T1_INTEGRATION_FILE" \
    > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-hash-registration-database.out"
  shasum -a 256 "$T1_ARCHITECTURE_FILE" \
    > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-hash-t1-argon2-worker-contract.out"
  grep -q "$T1_INTEGRATION_SHA" \
    "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-hash-registration-database.out" || failed=1
  grep -q "$T1_ARCHITECTURE_SHA" \
    "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-hash-t1-argon2-worker-contract.out" || failed=1

  stat -f "%N size=%z mtime=%m" "$T1_INTEGRATION_FILE" \
    > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-stat-registration-database.out"
  stat -f "%N size=%z mtime=%m" "$T1_ARCHITECTURE_FILE" \
    > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-stat-t1-argon2-worker-contract.out"

  T1_PATCHES_INSTALLED=0
  return $failed
}

# One exit path for every outcome. Restoration first, custody second, marker
# last — and restoration failure overrides everything that came before it.
t1_finish() {
  (( T1_FINISHED == 1 )) && return
  T1_FINISHED=1
  local incoming="${1:-}"

  t1_terminate_descendants

  if ! t1_restore; then
    print -r -- "CODEX BLOCKED (restoration)"
    [[ -n "$T1_TMP" && -d "$T1_TMP" ]] && rm -rf "$T1_TMP"
    exit 74
  fi

  # Custody re-verification, after restoration and before any marker.
  git rev-parse HEAD > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-head.out" 2>/dev/null
  grep -qx "$T1_HEAD" "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-head.out" || t1_block "custody"
  git diff --cached --name-only > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-index.out" 2>/dev/null
  [[ -s "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-index.out" ]] && t1_block "custody"
  shasum -a 256 ${T1_GOVERNED_PATHS[@]} > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-hashes.out" 2>/dev/null
  cmp -s "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-hashes.out" \
    "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-hashes.out" || t1_block "custody"
  git diff --check > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-whitespace.out" 2>&1
  git status --porcelain > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-worktree.out" 2>/dev/null
  t1_verify_descendants_gone || t1_block "custody"

  if [[ -n "$incoming" ]]; then t1_block "$incoming"; fi

  if [[ -n "$T1_BLOCK_REASON" ]]; then
    print -r -- "CODEX BLOCKED ($T1_BLOCK_REASON)"
    [[ -n "$T1_TMP" && -d "$T1_TMP" ]] && rm -rf "$T1_TMP"
    exit 2
  fi

  # Only a fully clean path may print a scientific marker, and only the one the
  # adjudicator computed.
  print -r -- "$T1_MARKER"
  [[ -n "$T1_TMP" && -d "$T1_TMP" ]] && rm -rf "$T1_TMP"
  exit 0
}

trap 't1_finish "custody"' INT TERM HUP QUIT
trap 't1_finish "custody"' EXIT

T1_PAIR_ARMS=(2 3  3 2  2 3  3 2  2 3  3 2  2 3  3 2  2 3  3 2)

t1_guard_status() {
  # $1 = raw status, $2 = cell name. 3 is the ruled 512 MiB safety stop and is
  # never mislabelled as an ordinary normal-cell failure.
  case "$1" in
    0) return 0 ;;
    3) t1_block "rss-safety"; t1_finish ;;
    *) t1_block "normal-cell"; t1_finish ;;
  esac
}

  # function call is a shell parameter, and what the child needs is an exported
  # environment entry. `env` makes that unambiguous.
  t1_run_cell "$cell" env "T1_N3_AB_WORKERS=$workers" "T1_N3_AB_CELL_ID=$cell" \
    NODE_OPTIONS=--expose-gc pnpm exec vitest run "$T1_INTEGRATION_FILE" \
      -t "$T1_TITLE_INTEGRATION" "${T1_VITEST_FLAGS[@]}"
  t1_guard_status "$?" "$cell"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 11. Mutants 1-7 against the installed temporary sources.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

t1_vitest_mutant() {
  local name="$1" file="$2" title="$3" workers="$4"
  local anchor="$5" expected="$6" replacement="$7"
  local slug
  [[ "$file" == "$T1_INTEGRATION_FILE" ]] && slug="integration" || slug="architecture"

  cp -p "$file" "$T1_TMP/$name-preimage.ts" || { t1_block "mutant"; t1_finish }
  shasum -a 256 "$T1_TMP/$name-preimage.ts" \
    > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name-preimage-hash.out"

  node "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-mutation-helper.mjs" \
    --source "$T1_TMP/$name-preimage.ts" --destination "$file" \
    --anchor "$anchor" --expected "$expected" --replacement "$replacement" \
    > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name-mutate.out" 2> "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name-mutate.err"
  t1_receipt "$?" "$name-mutate.status"
  grep -qx 0 "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name-mutate.status" || { t1_block "mutant"; t1_finish }

  T1_N3_AB_WORKERS="$workers" T1_N3_AB_CELL_ID="$name" NODE_OPTIONS=--expose-gc \
    t1_run_cell "$name" pnpm exec vitest run "$file" -t "$title" "${T1_VITEST_FLAGS[@]}"
  local mutant_status=$?

  cp -p "$T1_TMP/$name-preimage.ts" "$file"
  cmp "$file" "$T1_TMP/$name-preimage.ts"
  t1_receipt "$?" "$name-restore.status"

t1_adjudicator_mutant() {

# 13. Settle, restore, verify custody, THEN build and adjudicate.

t1_terminate_descendants

  print -r -- "CODEX BLOCKED (restoration)"

git rev-parse HEAD > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-head.out" 2>/dev/null
grep -qx "$T1_HEAD" "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-head.out" || { t1_block "custody"; t1_finish }
git diff --cached --name-only > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-index.out" 2>/dev/null

shasum -a 256 ${T1_GOVERNED_PATHS[@]} > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-hashes.out" 2>/dev/null
cmp -s "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-hashes.out" \
  "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-hashes.out" || { t1_block "custody"; t1_finish }
git diff --check > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-whitespace.out" 2>&1

(( $? == 0 )) || { t1_block "receipt"; t1_finish }

t1_run_cell "adjudication" node "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-adjudicator.mjs" \
  "T1-3worker-ab-manifest.json" --literal-carrier "$T1_CARRIER"
T1_ADJUDICATION_STATUS=$?

# The adjudicator's OWN stdout and stderr are scanned before its marker is

  "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-adjudication.err" 2>/dev/null; then

case "$T1_MARKER" in

  t1_block "receipt"
fi

# The carrier is destroyed here, before the single marker is printed and before
# the temporary directory is removed.
rm -f "$T1_CARRIER"

t1_finish

#!/bin/zsh
# T1 three-worker A/B — diagnostic runner.
#
# AUTHORING STATUS: design evidence for `T1-claude-3worker-ab-draft-packet.md`,
# authored under `T1-claude-3worker-ab-artifact-correction1-packet.md`. NEVER
# EXECUTED by the authoring seat. It becomes runnable only after two Sol xHigh
# reviewers approve this exact source AND V approves execution and records the
# final packet/artifact hashes in an external launch-authority file.
#
# WHAT THIS FILE IS
# The prior draft DESCRIBED signal handling, descendant tracking, the 512 MiB
# stop, unconditional restoration and the status override. A description cannot
# restore a governed test after a SIGINT. This file implements all of them, and
# the implementation is the point: every exit path — normal, failed, blocked,
# signalled — passes through `t1_finish`, which restores first, verifies custody
# second, and only then prints exactly one lawful marker.
#
# TWO ROOTS
# The outer Git root and the checkout root are different directories, and the
# prior draft conflated them: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the outer
# repository does NOT land where `apps/`, `packages/`, `tests/` and `pnpm` live.
# Both are verified here, and every repository-relative command runs after an
# explicit `cd` to the checkout.
#
# USAGE
#   zsh run-claude-T1-3worker-ab-diagnostic.sh <launch-authority.json>
#
# EXIT STATUS
#   0   one lawful scientific marker was printed
#   2   one lawful `CODEX BLOCKED (...)` marker was printed
#   74  custody or restoration failure; overrides every other outcome

set -u
setopt pipefail
unsetopt err_exit          # every cell's raw status must be captured, not fatal
setopt no_unset

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Roots. Verified before anything else, because every later path depends on
#    getting these two right.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

T1_OUTER_ROOT="/Users/vladmihaimiron/Documents/DebateAIRO"
T1_CHECKOUT_ROOT="$T1_OUTER_ROOT/dialectical-engine"
T1_LOGS_REL="docs/missions/2026-08-17-accounts-privacy-security/logs"
T1_LOGS="$T1_CHECKOUT_ROOT/$T1_LOGS_REL"

if [[ ! -d "$T1_OUTER_ROOT/.git" ]]; then
  print -r -- "CODEX BLOCKED (custody)"
  exit 74
fi
if [[ ! -d "$T1_CHECKOUT_ROOT/apps" || ! -d "$T1_CHECKOUT_ROOT/tests" || ! -d "$T1_LOGS" ]]; then
  print -r -- "CODEX BLOCKED (custody)"
  exit 74
fi
cd "$T1_CHECKOUT_ROOT" || { print -r -- "CODEX BLOCKED (custody)"; exit 74 }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Frozen constants.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

T1_HEAD="9801f85d97e4263a7c8311304e29d6a03c4a6d15"
T1_NODE_VERSION="v22.23.1"
T1_INTEGRATION_FILE="tests/integration/registration-database.test.ts"
T1_ARCHITECTURE_FILE="tests/architecture/t1-argon2-worker-contract.test.ts"
T1_INTEGRATION_SHA="7f8a048afaa415f49f340fe2ef15aa2d4140af1bbf3916bddf5353797a295c58"
T1_ARCHITECTURE_SHA="3548b93282011be73310efe8a2eec31638133dc69a1d92a0cf4ffbc36f253ca1"

T1_TITLE_INTEGRATION="T1 N3 AB three-worker credential concurrency diagnostic"
T1_TITLE_RESOURCE="T1 N3 AB architecture resource cell"
T1_TITLE_POSITIVE_CONTROL="T1 N3 AB retained allocation positive control"
T1_TITLE_FAULT_UNCONFIRMED="T1 N3 AB fault unconfirmed death"
T1_TITLE_FAULT_LATE_EXIT="T1 N3 AB fault late exit before close"
T1_TITLE_FAULT_RETRY="T1 N3 AB fault close-time termination retry fulfilled"

# An ARRAY, expanded as "${T1_VITEST_FLAGS[@]}". A scalar relying on word
# splitting is exactly how a flag with an `=` in it silently becomes two
# arguments — or one argument containing a space — under zsh's default settings.
T1_VITEST_FLAGS=(
  --pool=forks
  --poolOptions.forks.singleFork=true
  --no-file-parallelism
  --reporter=verbose
)

# The twelve governed paths, in the exact order the frozen hash list uses.
T1_GOVERNED_PATHS=(
  apps/api/src/index.ts
  apps/api/src/main.ts
  apps/api/src/registration.ts
  packages/crypto/src/index.ts
  packages/crypto/src/argon2-worker.ts
  packages/crypto/src/argon2-worker-pool.ts
  packages/db/src/identity.ts
  packages/register/src/auth-policy.ts
  tests/integration/registration-database.test.ts
  tests/unit/registration.test.ts
  tests/unit/argon2-worker-pool.test.ts
  tests/architecture/t1-argon2-worker-contract.test.ts
)

T1_ARTIFACTS=(
  T1-3worker-ab-booted-rss-harness.mjs
  T1-3worker-ab-adjudicator.mjs
  T1-3worker-ab-command-matrix.md
  T1-3worker-ab-integration.patch
  T1-3worker-ab-architecture.patch
  T1-3worker-ab-mutation-helper.mjs
  T1-3worker-ab-manifest-builder.mjs
  run-claude-T1-3worker-ab-diagnostic.sh
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Mutable run state.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

T1_TMP=""
T1_BACKUPS_TAKEN=0
T1_PATCHES_INSTALLED=0
T1_TRACKED_PIDS=()
T1_TRACKED_PGIDS=()
T1_BLOCK_REASON=""
T1_MARKER=""
T1_FINISHED=0

t1_receipt() { print -r -- "$1" > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$2" }

t1_block() {
  # First reason wins. A later custody failure never overwrites the safety stop
  # that caused it, and a scientific marker can never overwrite a block.
  [[ -z "$T1_BLOCK_REASON" ]] && T1_BLOCK_REASON="$1"
  print -r -- "$1" >> "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-block-reasons.out"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Descendant tracking, termination and reaping.
#
# Each cell runs in its OWN process group, so the whole subtree — Vitest, its
# fork pool, embedded PostgreSQL, worker threads' host processes — can be
# signalled as a unit. The wrapper's own PID is never in that group, which is
# why the final custody check can ask "are exactly these PGIDs gone?" instead of
# a host-wide `pgrep -f T1-3worker-ab` that would match this script, the editor
# that has it open and any unrelated work on the machine.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

t1_track() {
  T1_TRACKED_PIDS+=("$1")
  local pgid
  pgid=$(ps -o pgid= -p "$1" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ')
  [[ -n "$pgid" ]] && T1_TRACKED_PGIDS+=("$pgid")
}

t1_terminate_descendants() {
  local pgid
  for pgid in ${T1_TRACKED_PGIDS[@]}; do
    kill -TERM -"$pgid" 2>/dev/null
  done
  # A bounded grace period, then KILL. Sleeping is acceptable here precisely
  # because nothing else in this wrapper is running concurrently at this point.
  local waited=0
  while (( waited < 20 )); do
    local alive=0
    for pgid in ${T1_TRACKED_PGIDS[@]}; do
      kill -0 -"$pgid" 2>/dev/null && alive=1
    done
    (( alive == 0 )) && break
    sleep 0.5
    (( waited += 1 ))
  done
  for pgid in ${T1_TRACKED_PGIDS[@]}; do
    kill -KILL -"$pgid" 2>/dev/null
  done
  # Reap: the wrapper owns these jobs, so an unreaped zombie is the wrapper's.
  wait 2>/dev/null
}

t1_verify_descendants_gone() {
  local receipt="$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-descendants.out"
  : > "$receipt"
  local gone=0
  local pgid
  for pgid in ${T1_TRACKED_PGIDS[@]}; do
    if kill -0 -"$pgid" 2>/dev/null; then
      print -r -- "PGID=$pgid ALIVE" >> "$receipt"
    else
      print -r -- "PGID=$pgid GONE" >> "$receipt"
      (( gone += 1 ))
    fi
  done
  local pid
  for pid in ${T1_TRACKED_PIDS[@]}; do
    if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
      print -r -- "PID=$pid ALIVE" >> "$receipt"
    else
      print -r -- "PID=$pid GONE" >> "$receipt"
    fi
  done
  print -r -- "TRACKED_DESCENDANTS_GONE=$gone" >> "$receipt"
  grep -q "ALIVE" "$receipt" && return 1
  return 0
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Foreground cell execution.
#
# Foreground in the sense that matters: the wrapper waits for it and nothing
# else runs meanwhile. It is started with `setsid`-equivalent job control so it
# owns a process group, and its complete stdout, complete stderr and raw exit
# status land in three separate files.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

t1_run_cell() {
  local name="$1"; shift
  local out="$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name.out"
  local err="$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name.err"
  local sta="$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name.status"
  ( setopt monitor; exec "$@" ) > "$out" 2> "$err" &
  local pid=$!
  t1_track "$pid"
  wait "$pid"
  local status_code=$?
  print -r -- "$status_code" > "$sta"
  return $status_code
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Restoration and the final status override.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

t1_restore() {
  (( T1_BACKUPS_TAKEN == 1 )) || return 0
  local failed=0
  cp -p "$T1_TMP/registration-database.test.ts.bak" "$T1_INTEGRATION_FILE" || failed=1
  cp -p "$T1_TMP/t1-argon2-worker-contract.test.ts.bak" "$T1_ARCHITECTURE_FILE" || failed=1

  cmp "$T1_INTEGRATION_FILE" "$T1_TMP/registration-database.test.ts.bak"
  t1_receipt "$?" "restore-cmp-registration-database.status"
  grep -qx 0 "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-cmp-registration-database.status" || failed=1
  cmp "$T1_ARCHITECTURE_FILE" "$T1_TMP/t1-argon2-worker-contract.test.ts.bak"
  t1_receipt "$?" "restore-cmp-t1-argon2-worker-contract.status"
  grep -qx 0 "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-cmp-t1-argon2-worker-contract.status" || failed=1

  shasum -a 256 "$T1_INTEGRATION_FILE" \
    > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-hash-registration-database.out"
  shasum -a 256 "$T1_ARCHITECTURE_FILE" \
    > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-hash-t1-argon2-worker-contract.out"
  grep -q "$T1_INTEGRATION_SHA" \
    "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-hash-registration-database.out" || failed=1
  grep -q "$T1_ARCHITECTURE_SHA" \
    "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-hash-t1-argon2-worker-contract.out" || failed=1

  stat -f "%N size=%z mtime=%m" "$T1_INTEGRATION_FILE" \
    > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-stat-registration-database.out"
  stat -f "%N size=%z mtime=%m" "$T1_ARCHITECTURE_FILE" \
    > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-restore-stat-t1-argon2-worker-contract.out"

  T1_PATCHES_INSTALLED=0
  return $failed
}

# One exit path for every outcome. Restoration first, custody second, marker
# last — and restoration failure overrides everything that came before it.
t1_finish() {
  (( T1_FINISHED == 1 )) && return
  T1_FINISHED=1
  local incoming="${1:-}"

  t1_terminate_descendants

  if ! t1_restore; then
    print -r -- "CODEX BLOCKED (restoration)"
    [[ -n "$T1_TMP" && -d "$T1_TMP" ]] && rm -rf "$T1_TMP"
    exit 74
  fi

  # Custody re-verification, after restoration and before any marker.
  git rev-parse HEAD > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-head.out" 2>/dev/null
  grep -qx "$T1_HEAD" "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-head.out" || t1_block "custody"
  git diff --cached --name-only > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-index.out" 2>/dev/null
  [[ -s "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-index.out" ]] && t1_block "custody"
  shasum -a 256 ${T1_GOVERNED_PATHS[@]} > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-hashes.out" 2>/dev/null
  cmp -s "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-preflight-hashes.out" \
    "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-hashes.out" || t1_block "custody"
  git diff --check > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-whitespace.out" 2>&1
  git status --porcelain > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-final-worktree.out" 2>/dev/null
  t1_verify_descendants_gone || t1_block "custody"

  if [[ -n "$incoming" ]]; then t1_block "$incoming"; fi

  if [[ -n "$T1_BLOCK_REASON" ]]; then
    print -r -- "CODEX BLOCKED ($T1_BLOCK_REASON)"
    [[ -n "$T1_TMP" && -d "$T1_TMP" ]] && rm -rf "$T1_TMP"
    exit 2
  fi

  # Only a fully clean path may print a scientific marker, and only the one the
  # adjudicator computed.
  print -r -- "$T1_MARKER"
  [[ -n "$T1_TMP" && -d "$T1_TMP" ]] && rm -rf "$T1_TMP"
  exit 0
}

trap 't1_finish "custody"' INT TERM HUP QUIT
trap 't1_finish "custody"' EXIT

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. External launch authority. Absence or mismatch stops BEFORE any backup or
#    edit — the seat must never have touched a governed file on this path.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

T1_AUTHORITY="${1:-}"

t1_vitest_mutant() {
  local name="$1" file="$2" title="$3" workers="$4"
  local anchor="$5" expected="$6" replacement="$7"
  local slug
  [[ "$file" == "$T1_INTEGRATION_FILE" ]] && slug="integration" || slug="architecture"

  cp -p "$file" "$T1_TMP/$name-preimage.ts" || { t1_block "mutant"; t1_finish }
  shasum -a 256 "$T1_TMP/$name-preimage.ts" \
    > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name-preimage-hash.out"

  node "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-mutation-helper.mjs" \
    --source "$T1_TMP/$name-preimage.ts" --destination "$file" \
    --anchor "$anchor" --expected "$expected" --replacement "$replacement" \
    > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name-mutate.out" 2> "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name-mutate.err"
  t1_receipt "$?" "$name-mutate.status"
  grep -qx 0 "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name-mutate.status" || { t1_block "mutant"; t1_finish }

  t1_run_cell "$name" env "T1_N3_AB_WORKERS=$workers" "T1_N3_AB_CELL_ID=$name" \
    NODE_OPTIONS=--expose-gc pnpm exec vitest run "$file" -t "$title" "${T1_VITEST_FLAGS[@]}"
  local mutant_status=$?

  cp -p "$T1_TMP/$name-preimage.ts" "$file"
  cmp "$file" "$T1_TMP/$name-preimage.ts"
  t1_receipt "$?" "$name-restore.status"
  shasum -a 256 "$file" > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name-restore-hash.out"
  stat -f "%N size=%z mtime=%m" "$file" > "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name-restore-stat.out"
  grep -qx 0 "$T1_LOGS/T1-3worker-ab-$name-restore.status" \
    || { t1_block "restoration"; t1_finish }

  # A mutant that exits 0 has survived. A mutant with no status at all is not a
  # kill either: the builder refuses a missing or malformed status outright.
  (( mutant_status == 0 )) && { t1_block "mutant"; t1_finish }
  return 0
}

## 10. Vitest mutants 1-7

Each mutant is an anchor-bound, byte-exact, single-site replacement performed by
the hashed mutation helper on a pre-image copy of the INSTALLED temporary
source, written back over that source. The helper refuses zero matches, multiple
matches and any unexpected before-bytes, so a silent multi-site or drifted
replacement is impossible rather than merely unlikely.

Each block: hash the pre-image, mutate, run the exact named title, require a
nonzero status and the exact intended failure text, restore from the pre-image,
and verify hash, size, mtime and `cmp`.

## 14. Stop rules

The matrix stops — after letting active work settle, draining and closing — on
the FIRST of any of the following, and no failed cell is rerun in this seat:

| Condition | Marker |
|---|---|
| preflight, root, packet, artifact, hash, HEAD/index or descendant drift | `CODEX BLOCKED (custody)` |
| any generated literal or forbidden identifier in any stream | `CODEX BLOCKED (secret)` |
| any cell exits 3, the ruled 512 MiB diagnostic ceiling | `CODEX BLOCKED (rss-safety)` |
| either temporary test not restored byte-identically | `CODEX BLOCKED (restoration)` |
| a missing, truncated, empty, non-integer or unparseable receipt | `CODEX BLOCKED (receipt)` |
| any normal cell exits nonzero or fails a non-vacuity gate | `CODEX BLOCKED (normal-cell)` |
| any mutant survives, selects nothing, or fails to restore | `CODEX BLOCKED (mutant)` |

No early failure path prints a scientific marker. A blocked path records the
reason, terminates and reaps the tracked descendants, restores first, verifies
custody, and only then emits the one lawful `CODEX BLOCKED (...)` marker.
Restoration failure overrides every prior outcome with
`CODEX BLOCKED (restoration)` and status 74.

On a 512 MiB breach specifically the harness lets already-active work settle,
runs truthful cleanup, emits its structured secret-free safety report and exits
exactly 3; the wrapper maps that status to `CODEX BLOCKED (rss-safety)`, stops
every later three-worker cell, restores custody, and never mislabels it as
`normal-cell`.

The remaining outcomes are the four lawful scientific markers, emitted only by
the adjudicator and only after every gate above has passed:

- `THREE-WORKER A/B REPRODUCED AND SUPPORTS CREDENTIAL CONCURRENCY HYPOTHESIS`
- `THREE-WORKER A/B ORDINARY QUEUE SIGNATURE ONLY — HISTORICAL RED NOT REPRODUCED`
- `THREE-WORKER A/B CONTRADICTS CREDENTIAL CONCURRENCY HYPOTHESIS`
- `THREE-WORKER A/B MIXED OR INCONCLUSIVE`

No marker in either list authorizes production, changes provisional workers=2,
touches the permanent architecture exact-two gate, requalifies N*=3, amends the
384 MiB operator publication, approves Rework7-A, ratifies an RSS bound, or
moves Kanban to Done.

The stop-rule guard every executed cell is followed by. Status 3 is the ruled
512 MiB safety stop and is never mislabelled `normal-cell`:

```zsh
t1_guard() {

    *) t1_block "normal-cell"; t1_finish ;;
  esac
}
```

Every command below is foreground, captures complete stdout and complete stderr
into separate files, and writes its raw exit status into a third file. Every
executed cell runs in its own process group so the whole subtree can be
signalled and reaped as a unit.

## 10. Vitest mutants 1-7

Each mutant is an anchor-bound, byte-exact, single-site replacement performed by
the hashed mutation helper on a pre-image copy of the INSTALLED temporary
source, written back over that source. The helper refuses zero matches, multiple
matches and any unexpected before-bytes, so a silent multi-site or drifted
replacement is impossible rather than merely unlikely.

Each block: hash the pre-image, mutate, run the exact named title, require a
nonzero status and the exact intended failure text, restore from the pre-image,
and verify hash, size, mtime and `cmp`.

## 14. Stop rules

The matrix stops — after letting active work settle, draining and closing — on
the FIRST of any of the following, and no failed cell is rerun in this seat:

| Condition | Marker |
|---|---|
| preflight, root, packet, artifact, hash, HEAD/index or descendant drift | `CODEX BLOCKED (custody)` |
| any generated literal or forbidden identifier in any stream | `CODEX BLOCKED (secret)` |
| any cell exits 3, the ruled 512 MiB diagnostic ceiling | `CODEX BLOCKED (rss-safety)` |
| either temporary test not restored byte-identically | `CODEX BLOCKED (restoration)` |
| a missing, truncated, empty, non-integer or unparseable receipt | `CODEX BLOCKED (receipt)` |
| any normal cell exits nonzero or fails a non-vacuity gate | `CODEX BLOCKED (normal-cell)` |
| any mutant survives, selects nothing, or fails to restore | `CODEX BLOCKED (mutant)` |

No early failure path prints a scientific marker. A blocked path records the
reason, terminates and reaps the tracked descendants, restores first, verifies
custody, and only then emits the one lawful `CODEX BLOCKED (...)` marker.
Restoration failure overrides every prior outcome with
`CODEX BLOCKED (restoration)` and status 74.

On a 512 MiB breach specifically the harness lets already-active work settle,
runs truthful cleanup, emits its structured secret-free safety report and exits
exactly 3; the wrapper maps that status to `CODEX BLOCKED (rss-safety)`, stops
every later three-worker cell, restores custody, and never mislabels it as
`normal-cell`.

The remaining outcomes are the four lawful scientific markers, emitted only by
the adjudicator and only after every gate above has passed:

- `THREE-WORKER A/B REPRODUCED AND SUPPORTS CREDENTIAL CONCURRENCY HYPOTHESIS`
- `THREE-WORKER A/B ORDINARY QUEUE SIGNATURE ONLY — HISTORICAL RED NOT REPRODUCED`
- `THREE-WORKER A/B CONTRADICTS CREDENTIAL CONCURRENCY HYPOTHESIS`
- `THREE-WORKER A/B MIXED OR INCONCLUSIVE`

No marker in either list authorizes production, changes provisional workers=2,
touches the permanent architecture exact-two gate, requalifies N*=3, amends the
384 MiB operator publication, approves Rework7-A, ratifies an RSS bound, or
moves Kanban to Done.

# T1 three-worker A/B — exact command matrix

Date: 2026-08-22 (Europe/Bucharest)
Owner: Codex-Router / V
Kanban: `accounts-phase1` / `t_b225b2f2`
Status: **UNEXECUTED LEDGER — NOT A LAUNCH AUTHORIZATION**

## 0. What this document is

Every command the diagnostic seat may run, written out in full and in order. No
ellipses, no "repeat for the other nine pairs", no helper function standing in
for a cell. A reviewer who wants to know what will execute reads this file and
nothing else, and the seat that runs it copies lines rather than composing them.

This matrix is design evidence. It becomes runnable only after:

1. two Sol xHigh reviewers approve the exact source of
   `T1-3worker-ab-booted-rss-harness.mjs`, `T1-3worker-ab-adjudicator.mjs` and
   this file; and
2. V approves execution, with the finalized packet SHA-256 recorded externally
   in V's own approval record.

Nothing here selects three workers for production, amends policy, clears the
historical 973.0/1,264.7 ms N=3 failures, ratifies an RSS bound, or approves
Rework7-A.

## 1. Wrapper-owned environment

The wrapper — not the seat — establishes all of the following before the first
command in section 2, and owns them until the seat exits.

```sh
set -u
set -o pipefail
# NOT `set -e`: every cell's raw exit status must be captured and inspected, and
# an early shell exit would discard the status of the cell that failed.

T1_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cd "$T1_ROOT"

T1_LOGS="docs/missions/2026-08-17-accounts-privacy-security/logs"
T1_TMP="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/t1-n3-ab-XXXXXXXX")"

# The design-stage packet hash. The wrapper MUST verify the on-disk packet
# against the hash V approved externally before exporting this, and must abort
# with status 74 if they differ. The packet never contains its own hash, so this
# literal and V's approval record are the only two places it exists.
T1_SHA="a1cef6fb53a178607db9eb84036c7677d9aa0b8dffbb738b8da1873f4c047503"

T1_INTEGRATION_FILE="tests/integration/registration-database.test.ts"
T1_ARCHITECTURE_FILE="tests/architecture/t1-argon2-worker-contract.test.ts"

T1_TITLE_INTEGRATION="T1 N3 AB three-worker credential concurrency diagnostic"
T1_TITLE_RESOURCE="T1 N3 AB architecture resource cell"
T1_TITLE_FAULT_UNCONFIRMED="T1 N3 AB fault unconfirmed death"
T1_TITLE_FAULT_LATE_EXIT="T1 N3 AB fault late exit before close"
T1_TITLE_FAULT_RETRY="T1 N3 AB fault close-time termination retry fulfilled"
T1_TITLE_POSITIVE_CONTROL="T1 N3 AB retained allocation positive control"

T1_VITEST_FLAGS="--pool=forks --poolOptions.forks.singleFork=true --no-file-parallelism --reporter=verbose"
```

Wrapper obligations, restated because the matrix depends on all of them:

- track the complete Claude descendant process tree;
- on any signal, terminate and reap that tree BEFORE restoration;
- restore both temporary test files unconditionally on every exit path;
- verify SHA-256, size, mtime and `cmp` for both restored files;
- override any seat result with status 74 on custody failure.

Every command below is foreground. Every command captures complete stdout and
complete stderr into separate files and its raw exit status into a third file.
Every executed cell carries `T1_N3_AB_PACKET_SHA256="$T1_SHA"`.

## 10. Vitest mutants 1-7

Each mutant is a named single-site edit to a temporary test source, run against
its target title, expected to select at least one test and fail with the
intended text, then restored byte-identically from the wrapper's backup. Every
mutant is verified nonzero; a mutant that exits 0 is a survivor and a hard stop.

The mutation and restoration commands below use the same shape for all seven, so
the applied edit for each is stated explicitly before its command.

- mutant 01: the enqueue stamp is reported as the dispatch stamp.
- mutant 02: the settlement stamp is reported as the dispatch stamp.
- mutant 03: one credential job is omitted from the anonymous ordinal map.
- mutant 04: the three-worker cell secretly constructs two workers.
- mutant 05: the lifecycle observer reports `physicalAlive=4` (harness control).
- mutant 06: RSS is sampled only after settlement, never in flight.
- mutant 07: one worker warm-up is skipped.

## 13. Stop rules

The matrix stops — after letting active work settle, draining and closing — on
the FIRST of any of the following, and the seat does not rerun a failed cell:

| Condition | Marker |
|---|---|
| preflight, custody, hash, HEAD/index or process-tree drift | `CODEX BLOCKED (custody)` |
| any generated literal or forbidden identifier in any receipt | `CODEX BLOCKED (secret)` |
| any cell crosses the 512 MiB diagnostic ceiling | `CODEX BLOCKED (rss-safety)` |
| either temporary test not restored byte-identically | `CODEX BLOCKED (restoration)` |
| a missing, truncated or unparseable receipt | `CODEX BLOCKED (receipt)` |
| any normal cell exits nonzero or fails a non-vacuity gate | `CODEX BLOCKED (normal-cell)` |
| any mutant survives, selects nothing, or fails to restore | `CODEX BLOCKED (mutant)` |

On a 512 MiB breach specifically, the seat must let active work settle, close
cleanly, and run NO further three-worker cell. That is a safety stop ruled by V,
not an operator memory bound, and it does not become one.

The remaining outcomes are the four lawful scientific markers, emitted only by
the adjudicator and only after every gate above has passed:

- `THREE-WORKER A/B REPRODUCED AND SUPPORTS CREDENTIAL CONCURRENCY HYPOTHESIS`
- `THREE-WORKER A/B ORDINARY QUEUE SIGNATURE ONLY — HISTORICAL RED NOT REPRODUCED`
- `THREE-WORKER A/B CONTRADICTS CREDENTIAL CONCURRENCY HYPOTHESIS`
- `THREE-WORKER A/B MIXED OR INCONCLUSIVE`

No marker in either list authorizes production, changes provisional workers=2,
touches the permanent architecture exact-two gate, requalifies N*=3, amends the
384 MiB operator publication, approves Rework7-A, ratifies an RSS bound, or moves
Kanban to Done.
